expected_fail_detail.name: dfm::tests::thermal_via_side_round_absorbs_the_pow_vs_sqrt_divergence
expected_fail_detail.reason: Same root cause as pymath::tests::pow_is_not_a_multiply_or_a_sqrt -- it asserts the pow-vs-sqrt divergence is non-empty before checking that rounding absorbs it. Zero divergence on wasm32.

expected_fail_detail.name: dfm::tests::via_annular_area_uses_r_times_r_not_pow
expected_fail_detail.reason: Same root cause -- asserts r*r differs from pow(r,2.0) somewhere. Zero divergence on wasm32.

expected_fail_detail.name: pymath::tests::host_libm_symbols_actually_resolve
expected_fail_detail.reason: Asserts dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, ...) resolves cos/sin/acos/pow in the running process. wasm32 has no dynamic loader at all; pymath::dlsym_ptr is cfg'd to always miss there, because merely declaring the extern emits an env.dlsym import that makes the module non-instantiable in a bare isolate. The property under test is native-only by construction.

expected_fail_detail.name: pymath::tests::pow_is_not_a_multiply_or_a_sqrt
expected_fail_detail.reason: Asserts that libm pow(x,2.0) differs from x*x for at least one x out of 200000 samples, and pow(c,0.5) from sqrt(c). That divergence is what the B7 pin exists to preserve. On wasm32 pymath::pow falls back to f64::powf, which LLVM folds for constant exponents, so the divergence count is exactly zero and the staleness assertion fires. The test is correct; the platform property it pins is native-only.
